content.value_statement: Adding third-party libraries can create version drift and review risk. This skill guides approved dependency additions through catalog updates, version checks, and build verification.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a requested third-party dependency is necessary before adding it.
Requires user approval before dependency files are changed.
Looks up the latest stable library version before proposing an update.
Adds versions and library aliases to the Gradle version catalog.
Runs a relevant Gradle build or sync check after approved changes.
limitations: It assumes the project uses a Gradle version catalog.
It does not choose libraries without project context and user approval.
It does not perform a full supply chain or license audit.
It depends on current package registry or web search results.

use_cases.title: Add an Android Library
use_cases.description: Evaluate and add a justified library through the Gradle version catalog.

use_cases.title: Standardize Dependency Versions
use_cases.description: Keep dependency versions centralized while verifying build impact.

use_cases.title: Review Dependency Requests
use_cases.description: Check proposed dependency changes for approval, alternatives, and catalog consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add Retrofit to the project. Explain why it is needed, check the latest stable version, update the version catalog, and run relevant verification after I approve the change.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Alternatives
prompt_templates.prompt: Before adding a dependency, compare kotlinx.serialization and Moshi for this module. Recommend one option, explain the tradeoffs, and wait for approval before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Update Catalog Entry
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the approved image loading library to the Gradle version catalog. Use version and library aliases that match existing naming patterns, then verify the build.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Review Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the approved dependency, run the appropriate Gradle verification, and prepare a review summary covering need, alternatives, files changed, and build result.

output: Explains why the dependency is needed and what alternatives were considered.
Checks the latest stable release before proposing a catalog update.
Requests approval before editing dependency files.
Reports the build verification result after the approved change.

output_examples.input: Review whether a new date library is needed.
output_examples.output: States whether existing platform APIs are enough, summarizes alternatives, and asks for approval before any dependency change.

output_examples.input: Verify a dependency addition before review.
output_examples.output: Reports the verification task used, the result, and any follow-up needed for the code review.

best_practices: Get explicit user approval before editing dependency files.
Use the version catalog for versions and library aliases.
Run the smallest relevant build verification after changes.
anti_patterns: Adding a library before evaluating existing project code.
Hardcoding versions directly in Gradle build files.
Skipping verification after changing dependency metadata.

faq.question: What projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It is written for Gradle projects that manage dependencies through a version catalog.

faq.question: Does it fetch latest versions?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to check the latest stable release before proposing a dependency.

faq.question: Will it change build files?
faq.answer: It focuses on the version catalog and only changes module files when dependency usage requires it.

faq.question: Is user approval required?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires approval before adding a new third-party dependency.

faq.question: Does it assess license or security risk?
faq.answer: It prompts for justification and alternatives, but it does not perform a full supply chain audit.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is prepared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
